findings.criterion: clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal
findings.message: The North Star explicitly dictates that clicking ANY session tile opens a warm terminal. W3 and W6 introduce a 'Layer-1 warm view' that is just a non-PTY UI mock ('terminal chrome'), forcing a second click ('Resume live') to actually attach the live PTY. This 2-action bait-and-switch directly violates the 1-click 'opens a warm terminal' contract.

findings.criterion: Every Anchor session ... leaves an honest, machine-verified trail
findings.message: Wave 7 sets a post-deploy target of '>=90% Claude-engine sessions measured'. Designing the pipeline to tolerate a 10% failure/omission rate fundamentally breaks the North Star's absolute mandate that 'EVERY' session leaves a verified trail so numbers mean 'measured truth, not zero-by-omission'.

findings.criterion: clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal
findings.message: W6 defines an eviction path where reclaiming a worktree means clicking the tile spawns a 'NEW session' instead of resuming the parked one. While it chains the history, providing a fresh replacement session is not reliably opening the original session's 'warm terminal' as demanded for 'ANY' session tile.

W5 asserts that deduplicated doc-efforts contribute exactly 0. Adding a UI tooltip to explain why this specific effort is $0 (deduped vs actually free) would improve UX, but it does not trace to the North Star's strict requirements for machine-verified telemetry math.

The plan relies on 'eager finalize on EVERY end path' to snapshot usage, explicitly dictating that a later reconcile 'never reads the prunable home store'. If the Anchor process suffers a hard crash (OOM, SIGKILL, power loss), the end path never executes and the snapshot is never taken. Since reconcile is forbidden from checking the home store, the usage is permanently orphaned and drops from the rollup. Competitor tools stream or securely recover telemetry from crashes. This directly violates the North Star mandate of 'measured truth, not zero-by-omission'.

Wave 4 mandates taking a heartbeat snapshot piggybacked on the '120s autosave hook' and explicitly rules that a parse exception results in an atomic 'capture-failed' record. If the 120s heartbeat attempts to read the sidecar JSONL exactly while the engine is appending a new line, it will encounter a torn write, throw a parse exception, and permanently brand the active session as 'capture-failed'. Competitor telemetry tails active logs defensively; failing the entire session's cost capture on a concurrent read/write race is unacceptable.

The plan dictates 'no batch backfill job', relying exclusively on lazy generation upon the 'first open of a summary-less tile'. If an autonomous multi-agent wave spawns 50 one-shot jobs, the user must manually click 50 individual tiles just to trigger the summarization of what was accomplished. Competitor platforms auto-summarize wave outputs in the background. Hiding the 'what was accomplished' narrative behind manual per-tile clicks degrades the warm resume UX and obscures the project's state.

findings.criterion: clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal that narrates what was done
findings.message: The North Star explicitly mandates that 'clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal'. However, W6 introduces a '1-click/2-action path' where the first click only opens a static Layer-1 chrome view, requiring a second explicit 'Resume live' action to attach and swap in the actual live pane. This directly violates the 1-click warm terminal contract.

W4 states that engine_session_id capture will use either 'slug-dir watch... or PTY-banner parse per the W1 spike'. A Foreman-ready implementation plan must be completely deterministic; it cannot delegate architectural 'or' decisions to the build agent based on the outcome of an earlier wave's spike. This ambiguity blocks autonomous execution.

W4 mandates 'eager finalize on EVERY end path (kill, close/park...)'. When a ConPTY session is hard-killed, the underlying engine/sidecar may still be flushing the final tokens to disk. Eagerly reading the usage immediately on the kill path without a synchronization or flush-wait mechanism guarantees that the final turns of killed sessions will be silently undercounted, violating the 'not zero-by-omission' rule.

findings.criterion: Every Anchor session — interactive ConPTY or one-shot job — leaves an honest, machine-verified trail of what it cost
findings.message: W6 implements orientation as a 'read-only plan-mode one-shot job'. According to W4, one-shot jobs are routed into the usage ledger. If orientation is tracked as a standard one-shot job, clicking a tile multiple times will spawn multiple orientation jobs, inflating the project's total cost with read-only overhead. The plan must explicitly define how orientation job costs are classified or excluded from the primary effort rollup to avoid double-counting.
